a: One small item is stored in your browser to remember your cookie choice. If a booking or form provider is embedded (for example a calendar), it may set a session cookie needed for that embed to work; it is not used for tracking.

Google Analytics 4, used to count visits and see which pages are useful. The Google tag is on every page in a restricted mode (Google Consent Mode): until you accept, it sets no cookies and stores nothing on your device, and Google receives only anonymous, cookieless signals. If you accept, it sets first-party cookies (named _ga and _ga_*) so repeat visits can be recognised.

The LinkedIn Insight Tag, used on some pages to measure whether our LinkedIn campaigns work. It sets LinkedIn cookies and is loaded only after you accept on the cookie banner. No other advertising pixels or social-media trackers are used.
You can change your choice at any time with the ‘Cookie settings’ link in the footer, and clear cookies at any time in your browser settings. Questions to the email in the footer.
